introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - Advanced Level Examination. Information & Communication Technologies, Subject code 0796, Paper 3 (practical). Examination date: June 2021. Duration: two hours. The paper was set in two versions in the same document: Day 1 (booklet GCE/P/2021/0796/3/C/G1, workbook Trans-Business) and Day 2 (booklet GCE/P/2021/0796/3/C/G2, workbook Car Sales). Each version has the same three tasks.**

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. Do not write in pencil. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answer. Your results must be recorded in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Candidates must allow for themselves enough time to complete and check their work where these are required. The supervisor will guide you on how to save your files but usually you will be expected to save all your work in one folder named *Candidate folder* that will be created in your desktop. When an imperative programming language is required to write program code, either Standard [ISO] Pascal or [ANSI] C programming language may be used. You should ensure all your work is collected and printed before leaving the examination room. All printed work should be inserted in this booklet and well stapled. Carefully handle all equipment put at your disposal to avoid accidents that may lead to a disaster or system failure. Report any case of system or device malfunction to your supervisor.

**Answer ALL TASKS.**

Each version has three tasks: Task A (Databases, 21 marks), Task B (Spreadsheet, 19 marks) and Task C (Web Authoring Tool, 11 marks; printed as "Task 3").
enonce_intro_markdown:
**DAY 1**

**TASK C: WEB AUTHORING TOOL (11 marks)** *(printed as "Task 3")*

The design of a web page is given in the box below.

> **Four African Arab Countries** (centred heading)
>
> The African Arab countries are found in the northern part of African.
>
> The Arab countries are given below.
>
> 1. Egypt
> 2. Morocco.
> 3. Lybia
> 4. Tunisia

Write an HTML code to produce the expected webpage. Your code shall be evaluated following the guide.
incertitudes: Le PDF (8 pages, scan) contient DEUX versions du même sujet : « Day 1 » (pages 1 à 4, booklet GCE/P/2021/0796/3/C/G1, classeur Trans-Business) et « Day 2 » (pages 5 à 8, booklet G2, classeur Car Sales). Transcrites en six fichiers : numero_exercice D1-A, D1-B, D1-C et D2-A, D2-B, D2-C ; groupes ["DAY 1"] ou ["DAY 2"]. Le sujet n'imprime pas que chaque candidat n'en traite qu'une seule ; regles_choix reste donc vide.

Les fichiers de données du jour de l'examen (classeur Trans-Business ou Car Sales, feuilles Broker et Sales) ne sont pas dans le PDF. Leur structure est DÉDUITE du sujet : Broker (BrokerID, BrokerName, Town), Sales (SaleDate, BrokerID, CarCode, Quantity) ; feuille ESales : colonnes A à D = date, BrokerID, CarCode, quantité ; données en lignes 2 à 23 (plage A1:G23 imprimée), tableau récapitulatif à partir de A25 (en-tête ligne 25, courtiers lignes 26 à 35, total ligne 36). Les corrigés donnent des réponses génériques sur cette structure et invitent à l'adapter ; aucune valeur du classeur n'est inventée (seules des données fictives de contrôle, signalées comme telles).
Les « marking ideas » des corrigés sont des répartitions indicatives faites d'après les points imprimés ; le barème du jury n'est pas connu.

Vérifications : requêtes SQL exécutées avec sqlite3 sur données fictives (jointures Broker/Sales/Cars, filtre de dates, regroupement, intégrité référentielle) ; formules de tableur (LOOKUP/VLOOKUP, produit, 5 %, SUMIF) reproduites en Python sur 5 lignes fictives ; recherche approchée de LOOKUP simulée par une recherche dichotomique standard (le comportement exact d'Excel sur un vecteur non trié n'a pas été exécuté) ; HTML contrôlé par un analyseur Python (balises bien imbriquées), non affiché dans un navigateur. La syntaxe propre à Microsoft Access et Excel (assistants, menus, dates #m/j/aaaa#) est donnée de mémoire, non testée. Aucun code C ou Pascal n'est demandé dans ce paper : rien n'a été compilé.
Les titres des tâches sont imprimés « Task A », « Task B » puis « Task 3 » (faute d'impression) : la troisième tâche est transcrite sous le repère C et le titre imprimé est rappelé dans l'énoncé.

Barèmes : les points imprimés par question font 21 (tâche A), 19 (tâche B) et 11 (tâche C), conformes aux totaux imprimés, dans les deux versions. Les questions 5 (A) et 6 (B) comportent plusieurs lignes avec leurs propres points ; elles sont gardées en une seule question dont les points sont la somme (5 = 2 + 1 + 2 ; 6 = 2 + 2).

Day 1, tâche C : la maquette imprimée contient des fautes reproduites telles quelles dans le code du corrigé : « northern part of African » (au lieu de Africa), « Lybia » (au lieu de Libya), « Morocco. » avec un point final ; la consigne imprime « cantered header » (centered). La ligne « The Arab countries are given below. » est lue comme un second paragraphe, le « first paragraph » étant la phrase sous le titre.

questions.enonce_markdown: (a). The title of the page is Arab. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The title is declared in the head of the document with the `title` element:

```html
<head>
<title>Arab</title>
</head>
```

It is shown in the title bar (the tab) of the browser, not in the body of the page. Write it exactly as given: **Arab**.

Marking idea (2 marks): the title element placed in the head (1); with the right text (1).

The main heading uses the largest heading element, `h1`, and it is centred with the CSS property `text-align`: ```html

Four African Arab Countries

``` Equivalent older forms are `

` or `

...

`; they work in browsers but are deprecated in HTML5, so the CSS form is preferred. The heading text is the one of the design. Marking idea (2 marks): an h1 element with the heading text (1); centred (1).

The background colour of the page is set on the `body` element:

```html
<body style="background-color: grey;">
```

The same can be written in the head with a style sheet: `<style> body { background-color: grey; } </style>`. `grey` and `gray` are both valid colour names for the code `#808080`, which can be used instead (`background-color: #808080;`). The old attribute `bgcolor="grey"` also works but is deprecated.

Marking idea (2 marks): the colour applied to the body (1); the colour is grey (1).

The first paragraph is the sentence under the heading. A paragraph is written with the `p` element: ```html

The African Arab countries are found in the northern part of African.

``` The text is typed as it is printed in the design. (The following line of the design, *The Arab countries are given below.*, is a second paragraph, `

The Arab countries are given below.

`, placed just before the list.) The design prints "northern part of African" (the correct form is "northern part of Africa"); the code reproduces the design. Marking idea (2 marks): the p element (1); with the text of the design (1).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(e). The ordered list. *[3 marks]*

**Save your web page as Arab.html and print a copy.**
questions.corrige_markdown:
A numbered list is an ordered list: the `ol` element holds one `li` element per item, and the browser writes the numbers 1 to 4 itself: ```html
  1. Egypt
  2. Morocco.
  3. Lybia
  4. Tunisia
``` The items are typed as in the design ("Egypt", "Morocco.", "Lybia", "Tunisia"); the full stop printed after one of them belongs to the item as printed. **Complete page, to save as `Arab.html`:** ```html Arab

Four African Arab Countries

The African Arab countries are found in the northern part of African.

The Arab countries are given below.

  1. Egypt
  2. Morocco.
  3. Lybia
  4. Tunisia
``` **Saving and printing.** In a text editor (Notepad) choose *File* > *Save As*, *Save as type: All Files*, file name `Arab.html`, in the candidate folder. Open the file in a web browser to check the title in the tab, the centred heading, the grey background, the paragraph and the numbered list, then print the page (Ctrl+P) and staple the copy in the booklet. Marking idea (3 marks): the ol element (1); one li element for each of the four items (1); file saved under the right name and a copy printed (1). (The structure of this page was checked with a Python parser: every tag is opened and closed in the right order. It was not displayed in a browser.)
